title: Stevioside Alleviates Con A-Induced Liver Injury by Activating the AMPK/NRF2 Signaling Pathway.
authors: Zhang, Zhe; Wang, Yidan; Hu, Jinping; Zhang, Yuxin; Qiu, Lingling; Wang, Baoyin; Zhang, Xiwen; Ding, Yu; Ren, Wenzhi; Jin, Hongjuan; Yuan, Bao
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
one_liner_zh: 该文研究甜菊苷通过AMPK/NRF2通路缓解Con A诱导肝损伤，核心是药物-蛋白互作与信号通路，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Stevioside is a natural sweetener extracted from the perennial herb Stevia rebaudiana and has been approved by the FDA as an important dietary supplement. In addition, it possesses anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antiapoptotic properties. Nevertheless, its therapeutic efficacy against concanavalin A (Con A)-induced liver injury remains unclear. This study was designed to investigate the protective effect of stevioside on Con A-induced liver injury and to elucidate the underlying mechanisms. Using a Con A-induced mouse liver injury model, we evaluated liver damage via serum biochemistry and histopathology, identified key pathways through hepatic transcriptomics, and validated direct targets with molecular docking, CETSA, and DARTS assays. Compared with the model group, stevioside treatment dose-dependently reduced serum levels of hepatic injury markers and markedly ameliorated histopathological damage. Moreover, stevioside attenuated Con A-triggered hepatitis and hepatocyte apoptosis. Hepatic transcriptomic analyses revealed that differentially expressed genes were enriched in processes related to oxidoreductase activity, and stevioside effectively alleviated hepatic oxidative stress. Molecular docking, CETSA, and DARTS assays further identified AMPK may be the critical target for stevioside. In vitro experiments showed that stevioside suppressed Con A-induced inflammation and oxidative stress in RAW264.7 cells. In vivo, genetic knockout of Nrf2 or pharmacological inhibition of AMPK markedly diminished the hepatoprotective effects of stevioside. Collectively, stevioside activated the AMPK/NRF2 signaling pathway through its interaction with AMPK, thereby exerting hepatoprotective effects. Our study not only provides a theoretical basis for the application of stevioside in preventing liver diseases, but also opens new avenues for the treatment of liver injury.
abstract_zh: Stevioside是一种从多年生草本植物甜叶菊（Stevia rebaudiana）中提取的天然甜味剂，并已被FDA批准作为重要的膳食补充剂。此外，它具有抗炎、抗氧化和抗凋亡特性。然而，其对刀豆蛋白A（Con A）诱导的肝损伤的治疗效果仍不清楚。本研究旨在探讨Stevioside对Con A诱导肝损伤的保护作用，并阐明其潜在机制。利用Con A诱导的小鼠肝损伤模型，我们通过血清生化学和组织病理学评估肝损伤，通过肝脏转录组学识别关键通路，并通过分子对接、CETSA和DARTS实验验证直接靶点。与模型组相比，Stevioside治疗剂量依赖性地降低了肝损伤标志物的血清水平，并显著改善了组织病理学损伤。此外，Stevioside减轻了Con A触发的肝炎和肝细胞凋亡。肝脏转录组学分析显示，差异表达基因富集于与氧化还原酶活性相关的过程，且Stevioside有效缓解了肝脏氧化应激。分子对接、CETSA和DARTS实验进一步表明AMPK可能是Stevioside的关键靶点。体外实验显示，Stevioside抑制了Con A诱导的RAW264.7细胞中的炎症和氧化应激。在体内，Nrf2的基因敲除或AMPK的药理学抑制显著减弱了Stevioside的肝保护作用。总之，Stevioside通过其与AMPK的相互作用激活AMPK/NRF2信号通路，从而发挥肝保护作用。我们的研究不仅为Stevioside在预防肝脏疾病中的应用提供了理论基础，也为肝损伤的治疗开辟了新途径。
